assumptions: All model behavior is offline and synthetic; the server never calls a provider.

assumptions.input_accounting: Each call adds ceil(UTF-8 template bytes / chars_per_token) to the separately declared argument bounds.
assumptions.output_assumption: The oracle emits no more than the resolved model contract's declared max_tokens cap.
assumptions.input_assumption: For every complete request, target-model input usage is at most the sum of the template estimate and declared argument bounds. chars_per_token is a UTF-8 byte divisor; provider tokenizers, request envelopes, and tokenization boundary effects are not modeled.
assumptions.note: These are explicit abstract accounting assumptions, not a guarantee about real provider billing.

guarantee_scope.property: paired billing-trace equality under the stated abstract model
guarantee_scope.oracle_coupling: Paired executions share abstract responses under Ω(M,k,Q) when resolved contract M, per-contract ordinal k, retry outcomes, and the complete modeled request Q match. The default ordinal mock ignores Q in its output projection; --request-sensitive-oracle adds decoded template bytes, ordered literal bytes, and identifier Value(tokens,flag) fields to Q. This models no real provider request text.
guarantee_scope.token_usage: Input use follows the summed UTF-8 template and declared argument bounds; output use respects the resolved contract's max_tokens cap.
guarantee_scope.relational_obligations: A discharged entry records a local structural request-trace comparison. It is not by itself a universal whole-workflow claim.
guarantee_scope.declassification: This workflow contains no declassification; the claim is still conditional on the stated shared-oracle and abstract token-accounting assumptions.
